setup: Stand tall, bar resting on your thighs
execution: Lead with your elbows, out to the sides
Lift the bar close to your body
Stop when your elbows reach shoulder height
faults: Don't pull your elbows above your shoulders
Don't let your wrists lead the bar

notes: Many lifters find the top of this lift uncomfortable on the shoulders. Keep the weight moderate, and stop the elbows at about shoulder height or lower if that feels better.
An EZ bar, or a grip a little wider than shoulder width, is often more comfortable on the wrists and shoulders.
Log the total including the bar. EZ bars and Olympic bars weigh different amounts, so loads aren't comparable between them.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Elbows raised out to the sides to about shoulder height, higher than the hands. Bar close to the body at lower-chest level. Shoulders not shrugged to the ears.

ikHints: Bar stays close to the body

Elbows stop at about shoulder height
